# ============================================== #
# simple cleaning

# glimpse(rt)
# glimpse(rt2)


cols_upper <- c("recorder_name",
                "reference_no",
                "study_area",
                "specific_area",
                "taxonomic_unit",
                "taxonomic_unit_revised")



rt2 <- rt %>% 
  # convert space in columns to underbar
  rename_with(~ .x %>%
                str_replace_all(" ", "_") %>%
                str_to_lower()) %>% 
  
  # convert text to lower (except specified columns)
  mutate(across(c(where(is.character),
                  -all_of(cols_upper)),
                str_to_lower)) %>% 
  
  # replace NA with "na"
  mutate(across(everything(),
                ~ tidyr::replace_na(.x, "na")))

# glimpse(rt2)



# ============================================== #
# filter out irrelevant data at initial stage
# edit start period and end period data

rt2$include %>% unique() %>% sort()
[1] 0 1 2
Code 
rt3 <- rt2 %>% 
  filter(
    # this include col was made in excel for rows based on:
    # n_years: too large (comparison with glacial time)
    # gradient = na
    # magnitude_of_shift = na
    # notes = no resurvey
    # include == 2 is "pending" literature
    include %in% 1) %>%
  
  # start period
  rename(startperiod_orig = start_period) %>%
  mutate(
    # extract all 4-digit years
    startperiod_years = str_extract_all(startperiod_orig, "\\d{4}"),
    
    startperiod_startyear = map_int(
      startperiod_years,
      ~ ifelse(length(.x) == 0, NA_integer_, as.integer(.x[1]))
    ),
    
    startperiod_endyear = map_int(
      startperiod_years,
      ~ ifelse(length(.x) == 0, NA_integer_, as.integer(.x[length(.x)]))
    ),
    
    startperiod_midyear = (startperiod_startyear + startperiod_endyear) / 2
  ) %>%
  select(-startperiod_years) %>% 
  relocate(startperiod_startyear, startperiod_endyear, startperiod_midyear, .after = startperiod_orig) %>% 
  
  # end period
  rename(endperiod_orig = end_period) %>%
  mutate(
    # extract all 4-digit years
    endperiod_years = str_extract_all(endperiod_orig, "\\d{4}"),
    
    endperiod_startyear = map_int(
      endperiod_years,
      ~ ifelse(length(.x) == 0, NA_integer_, as.integer(.x[1]))
    ),
    
    endperiod_endyear = map_int(
      endperiod_years,
      ~ ifelse(length(.x) == 0, NA_integer_, as.integer(.x[length(.x)]))
    ),
    
    endperiod_midyear = (endperiod_startyear + endperiod_endyear) / 2
  ) %>%
  select(-endperiod_years) %>% 
  relocate(endperiod_startyear, endperiod_endyear, endperiod_midyear, .after = endperiod_orig) %>% 
  
  # n_years
  mutate(
    n_years_midyear = endperiod_midyear - startperiod_midyear
  ) %>% 
  relocate(n_years_midyear, .after = n_years)

# minor edits

# glimpse(ref_en)
# glimpse(ref_ja)

ref_en2 <- ref_en %>% 
  # convert space in columns to underbar
  rename_with(~ .x %>%
                str_replace_all(" ", "_") %>%
                str_to_lower())

ref_ja2 <- ref_ja %>% 
  # convert space in columns to underbar
  rename_with(~ .x %>%
                str_replace_all(" ", "_") %>%
                str_to_lower())


# glimpse(ref_en2)
# glimpse(ref_ja2)


ref_en3 <- ref_en2 %>% 
  filter(reference_no %in% unique(rt3$reference_no)) %>% 
  select(reference_no, article_title, data_section, source_title, publication_year, authors, doi) %>% 
  mutate(publication_year = as.numeric(publication_year),
         language = "English")

ref_ja3 <- ref_ja2 %>% 
  filter(reference_no %in% unique(rt3$reference_no)) %>% 
  select(reference_no, article_title, data_section, source_title, publication_year, authors, doi) %>% 
  mutate(language = "Japanese")

                      ref_ja3) %>% 
  relocate(language, reference_no, doi, authors, article_title, publication_year, source_title, data_section) %>% 
  mutate(author_year = str_c(authors, publication_year, sep = " "))

  "leading edge" = "leading edge",
  "leading" = "leading edge",
  "northern limit" = "leading edge",
  "前縁" = "leading edge",
  
  # centroid
  "centroid" = "centroid",
  "centroid / multiple sites" = "centroid",
  
  "average" = "centroid", # Dai E0434 pika: study is about centroid
  "na" = "centroid", # Nonaka J0202 sika: authors do not mention centroid, but the study area covers entire honshu, shikoku, and kyushu, which largely covers the sika's distribution. so centroid was applied here.
  
  # need to check using distribution data, but it will be converted to centroid for now, because it is likely to reflect the centroid
  "unknown" = "centroid", # Sakiyama E0009
  
  # trailing edge
  "trailing edge" = "trailing edge",
  "trailing" = "trailing edge",
  
  
  # check
  "前縁、重心、後縁" = "others" # Nonaka J0201 bird: authors do not mention but this can be interpreted as centroid


)

    ),

    ),

    ),
    
    # n_years = recode(
    #   n_years,
    #   !!!nyears_recode
    # ),
    
    number_of_censuses = recode(
      number_of_censuses,
      !!!ncensus_recode
    ),

    #   magnitude_of_shift,
    #   !!!magshift_recode
    # ),
    
    unit_of_shift = recode(
      unit_of_shift,

    ),

    magnitude_of_shift = na_if(magnitude_of_shift, "na"),
    magnitude_of_shift = as.numeric(magnitude_of_shift)
    
  ) %>% 
  relocate(realm, .after = "ecosystem") %>% 
  relocate(observation, .after = "measurement_type") %>% 
  
  # ecosystem order
  mutate(
    
    # check entry with ecosystem_recode %>% unique()
    
    ecosystem = factor(
      ecosystem,
      levels = c(
        "alpine",

    realm = factor(

        "marine"
        )
    ),
    gradient = factor(
      gradient,
      levels = c(
        "elevation",
        "latitude",
        "longitude",
        "horizontal")
    )
  ) %>% 
  
  left_join(ref_bind2 %>% select(-language),
            by = "reference_no")

# ------------ #
# conversion from latitude degrees to km
latdeg_to_km <- function(deg) {
  earth_radius <- 6371
  deg * 2 * pi * earth_radius / 360
}

# ---- #
# example 

latdeg_to_km(0.1)
[1] 11.11949
Code 
# ---- #



# ------------ #
# conversion from longitude degrees to km
londeg_to_km <- function(deg, latitude) {
  earth_radius <- 6371
  deg * 2 * pi * earth_radius / 360 * cos(latitude * pi / 180)
}

# ---- #
# example

londeg_to_km(1, latitude = 36)
[1] 89.95859
Code 
londeg_to_km(1, latitude = 46)
[1] 77.24249

# ---- #

# lat mean for longitude studies
lon_latrange2 <- lon_latrange %>% 
  rename_with(~ .x %>%
                str_replace_all(" ", "_") %>%
                str_to_lower()) %>% 
  # convert text to lower (except specified columns)
  mutate(gradient = str_to_lower(gradient)) %>% 
  filter(include == 1) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(lat_mean = mean(lat_min, lat_max)) %>% 
  select(reference_no, gradient, lat_mean)
  






# ------------ #
rt5 <- rt4 %>% 
  
  left_join(lon_latrange2, 
            by = c("reference_no", "gradient")) %>% 
  
  # transform magnitudeshift and unitshift
  mutate(
    
    magnitude_of_shift = case_when(
      
      # apply these to magnitudeshift depending on
      # gradient
      # unitshift
      
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      # elevation --> m/year
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      
      # m --> m/year
      gradient == "elevation" & unit_of_shift == "m" ~
        magnitude_of_shift / n_years_midyear,
      
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      # latitude --> km/year
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      
      # degree --> km --> km/year
      gradient == "latitude" & unit_of_shift == "degree" ~
        latdeg_to_km(magnitude_of_shift) / n_years_midyear,
      
      # degree/year --> km/year
      gradient == "latitude" & unit_of_shift == "degree/year" ~
        latdeg_to_km(magnitude_of_shift),
      
      # km --> km/year
      gradient == "latitude" & unit_of_shift == "km" ~
        magnitude_of_shift / n_years_midyear,
      
      # already km/year
      gradient == "latitude" & unit_of_shift == "km/year" ~
        magnitude_of_shift,
      
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      # longitude --> km/year
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      
      # degree --> km --> km/year
      gradient == "longitude" & unit_of_shift == "degree" ~
        londeg_to_km(magnitude_of_shift, latitude = lat_mean) / n_years_midyear,
      
      # degree/year --> km/year
      gradient == "longitude" & unit_of_shift == "degree/year" ~
        londeg_to_km(magnitude_of_shift, latitude = lat_mean),
      
      
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      # horizontal --> km/year
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      
      # km --> km/year
      gradient == "horizontal" & unit_of_shift == "km" ~
        magnitude_of_shift / n_years_midyear,
      
      # already km/year
      gradient == "horizontal" & unit_of_shift == "km/year" ~
        magnitude_of_shift,
      
      
      # anything unexpected
      TRUE ~ NA_real_

    ),
    
    unit_of_shift = case_when(
      gradient == "elevation" ~ "m/year",
      gradient %in% c("latitude", "longitude", "horizontal") ~ "km/year",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
      )
    )



# ------------ #
# check combination of gradient and unit
rt5 %>%
  distinct(gradient, unit_of_shift) %>%
  arrange(gradient, unit_of_shift)

  gradient   unit_of_shift

1 elevation  m/year       
2 horizontal km/year      
3 latitude   km/year      
4 longitude  km/year

[11] "changed \"number of censuses\" column from 632 to 257 as the study presented the effort per species."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
[12] "changed \"number of censuses\" column from 632 to 285 as the study presented the effort per species."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
[13] "magnitudeofshift, unitofshift, and shiftsource columns were recalculated after confirming with takahashi-san."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
[14] "edited the entry for magnitude after recalculation. shift was computable for both latitude and longitude so the row was duplicated. the shift was calculated using the latitude and longitude coordinates of the cities based on table 1 and figure 1, of which the error is marginal considering thelarge extent of the study (western japan was the study area and sampling locations were indicated by city names). information on number of censuses was not provided in the literature. we assigned 39 for this column to present the number of studies that this e2247 study referred to build the species distribution records, based on the table 1, considering that one set of distribution survey (census) was conducted per study."
[15] "edited magnitudeofshift as 5.8 using the median value of range shift in sika. the unit was edited to km, which was originally written in japanese."

 [5] "na"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
 [6] "number of censuses refer to total number of occurrences used for calculating the shifts (both coasts and all years)"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
 [7] "shifts calculated as least coast path distances along the coast between reported northernmost records between periods"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
 [8] "shifts estimated as the slope coefficient of the linear regression fitted to the annual lat and lon of centroids provided in sup. table s1. the significance test corresponds to the p-value of the regression slope (significant if p-value <= 0.05). azimuths (bearings) calculated from the initial and final coordinates of the centroid in the series."                                              
 [9] "while the study focuses on the korean waters, this study was included because it mainly focuses on open sea species from the surrounding seas of japan. range shift was estimated by extracting data from the plots. the measurement of fish data was biomass. the latitude represents biomass-weighted monthly mean latitudes."                                                                          
[10] "centriod in deapth and temperature gradient were also provided. length of the latitudinal shift was read from the figure showing 16 years regression line (trend analysis). caution is needed since this trend analyses ignores time autocorrelation (e.g., correlation between latitude centroid and calender year)."                                                                                    
[11] "the shift was stated in fig. 5 and esm4 for each species showing long term trend value."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
[12] "shifts estimated from fig. 3. the significance tested corresponds to the overall centroid shift not the lat/lon ones as stated in the paper. azimuths (bearings) calculated from the lat/lon shifts."                                                                                                                                                                                                     
[13] "shifts provided as minimum estimates of expansion rates over the period"

[15] "the shift change was estimated from fig. 4 using webplotdigitzer (https://automeris.io/wpd/?v=5_2)"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
[16] "fig 3 was used for extracting the latitude and year information and then linear regression was used to compute the significance of the shift."

# ============================================== #
# bar plot: count rows per ecosystem x x gradient

rt_temp <- rt_cleaned %>%
  
  filter(
    !is.na(magnitude_of_shift)
  ) %>%
  
  count(
    gradient,
    ecosystem,
    realm
  )

ggplot(rt_temp, aes(x = realm, y = n, fill = ecosystem)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  facet_grid2(
    . ~ gradient,
    scales = "free_x",
    independent = "x"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Realm",
    y = "Number of observations",
    fill = "Ecosystem",
    title = "Number of observations per gradient",
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )

Gantt chart-like plot

1: row height varies with sample size

Code 
# ============================================== #
# Gantt chart-like plot of study duration per observation

rt_temp <- rt_cleaned %>%
  
  filter(
    !is.na(startperiod_midyear),
    !is.na(endperiod_midyear)
  ) %>%
  
  group_by(realm, publication_id) %>%
  mutate(
    publication_start = min(startperiod_midyear, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  arrange(
    realm,
    publication_start,
    publication_id,
    startperiod_midyear,
    endperiod_midyear
  ) %>%
  
  # publication legend follows arranged order
  mutate(
    publication_id = factor(
      publication_id,
      levels = unique(publication_id)
    ),
    
    # unique observation ID across whole dataset
    obs_id = row_number()
  )%>%
  mutate(
    census_linetype = case_when(
      number_of_censuses == 2 ~ "2 censuses",
      TRUE ~ ">2 censuses"
    )
  )


n_pub <- nlevels(rt_temp$publication_id)

publication_colors <- colorspace::qualitative_hcl(
  n_pub,
  palette = "Dark 3"
)

publication_colors <- publication_colors[
  c(
    seq(1, n_pub, by = 2),
    seq(2, n_pub, by = 2)
  )
]


class(rt_temp$obs_id)

Code 
# ============================================== #
# Gantt chart-like plot of study duration per observation
#
# Equal vertical height for:
#   1. each realm
#   2. each reference within each realm


rt_temp <- rt_cleaned %>%
  
  filter(
    !is.na(startperiod_midyear),
    !is.na(endperiod_midyear)
  ) %>%
  
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # First year represented by each publication
  
  group_by(realm, publication_id) %>%
  mutate(
    publication_start = min(
      startperiod_midyear,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # Arrange publications and observations
  
  arrange(
    realm,
    publication_start,
    publication_id,
    startperiod_midyear,
    endperiod_midyear
  ) %>%
  
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # Publication factor follows arranged order
  
  mutate(
    publication_id = factor(
      publication_id,
      levels = unique(publication_id)
    )
  ) %>%
  
  
  # ============================================== #
  # Give each reference an equal-height band
  # within each realm
  
  group_by(realm) %>%
  mutate(
    
    # reference order within realm
    reference_order = match(
      publication_id,
      unique(publication_id)
    ),
    
    # number of references in realm
    n_ref_realm = n_distinct(publication_id)
    
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # Give each observation a position within
  # its reference band
  
  group_by(realm, publication_id) %>%
  mutate(
    
    n_entry = n(),
    obs_order = row_number(),
    
    # center of this reference's band
    reference_center = (
      reference_order - 0.5
    ) / n_ref_realm,
    
    # total vertical height available
    # to this reference
    reference_height = 1 / n_ref_realm,
    
    # observation positions within reference band
    #
    # observations occupy 70% of the available
    # reference band (±35% around the center)
    obs_offset = if (n() == 1) {
      
      0
      
    } else {
      
      (
        (obs_order - 1) / (n_entry - 1) - 0.5
      ) * 0.7 * first(reference_height)
      
    },
    
    # final y position
    obs_y = reference_center + obs_offset
    
  ) %>%
  
  ungroup() %>%
  
  mutate(
    realm = factor(
      realm,
      levels = c("terrestrial", "marine"),
      labels = c("Terrestrial", "Marine")
    ),
    census_linetype = case_when(
      number_of_censuses == 2 ~ "2 censuses",
      TRUE ~ ">2 censuses"
    )
  )


# ============================================== #
# Reference labels
#
# Because each reference now has its own
# equal-height band, simply use reference_center
# as the label position.


publication_labels <- rt_temp %>%
  
  group_by(
    realm,
    publication_id
  ) %>%
  
  summarise(
    label_y = first(reference_center),
    n_entry = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  mutate(
    publication_label = as.character(publication_id),
    
    publication_label = case_when(
      
      # References containing "et al."
      stringr::str_detect(publication_label, " et al\\. ") ~
        stringr::str_replace(
          publication_label,
          "^(.*?) et al\\. (.*)$",
          "'\\1 '*italic('et al.')*' \\2'"
        ),
      
      # References without "et al."
      TRUE ~ paste0(
        "'",
        publication_label,
        "'"
      )
    ),
    
    # Add italic (n = x)
    publication_label = paste0(
      publication_label,
      "*' ('*italic(n == ",
      n_entry,
      ")*')'"
    )
  )


# ============================================== #
# Publication colors


n_pub <- nlevels(rt_temp$publication_id)

publication_colors <- colorspace::qualitative_hcl(
  n_pub,
  palette = "Dark 3"
)

publication_colors <- publication_colors[
  c(
    seq(1, n_pub, by = 2),
    seq(2, n_pub, by = 2)
  )
]


# ============================================== #
# Plot


ggplot(
  rt_temp,
  aes(
    y = obs_y,
    color = publication_id
  )
) +
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # Study period
  
  geom_segment(
    aes(
      x = startperiod_midyear,
      xend = endperiod_midyear,
      yend = obs_y,
      linetype = census_linetype
    ),
    linewidth = 1,
    alpha = 1
  ) +
  
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # Plus sign at first survey year
  
  geom_text(
    aes(
      x = startperiod_midyear,
      y = obs_y
    ),
    label = "+",
    color = "black",
    size = 4,
    vjust = 0.35,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # Plus sign at final survey year
  
  geom_text(
    aes(
      x = endperiod_midyear,
      y = obs_y
    ),
    label = "+",
    color = "black",
    size = 4,
    vjust = 0.35,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # Reference labels
  
  geom_text(
    data = publication_labels,
    aes(
      x = -Inf,
      y = label_y,
      label = publication_label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    parse = TRUE,
    hjust = 1.05,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  
  
  # ============================================== #
  # Scales
  
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "2 censuses" = "longdash",
      ">2 censuses" = "solid"
    )
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = publication_colors
  ) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0.02, 0.02)
    )
  ) +
  
  scale_y_reverse(
    limits = c(1.02, -0.02),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  
  
  # ============================================== #
  # Equal-height realm facets
  
  facet_grid2(
    rows = vars(realm),
    scales = "fixed",
    space = "fixed"
  ) +
  
  
  coord_cartesian(
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  
  
  labs(
    x = "Year of record",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  
  
  guides(
    color = "none",
    linetype = "none"
  ) +
  
  
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.text.y.right = element_text(angle = 0),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90"),
